title: Work & colleagues
goal: Chat with colleagues, talk to your boss in the right register, handle deadlines and meetings, ask for leave and get through a job interview.
intro:
Office Odia is two languages at once. Between colleagues it is relaxed and full of English — **ମିଟିଂ**, **ଇମେଲ୍**, **ଡେଡଲାଇନ୍** — with Odia verbs doing the grammar. With the boss, in a government office or in writing it shifts to **formal Odia**: ଆପଣ forms throughout, **ସାର୍ / ମ୍ୟାଡାମ୍** or **ଆଜ୍ଞା**, and words like **ଆବଶ୍ୟକ** and **ଜଣାଇବା** instead of ଦରକାର and କହିବା.

This unit puts both side by side, and adds the **passive** you meet in emails and notices: **ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ନିଆଗଲା** 'it was decided', **ରିପୋର୍ଟ ପଠାଯାଇଛି** 'the report has been sent', and the handy **କରି ହେବ ନାହିଁ** 'it can't be done'.

vocab.note: Everyday word. ମିଟିଂ ଅଛି 'there's a meeting', ମିଟିଂରେ ଅଛି 'I'm in a meeting'. Formal: ବୈଠକ.
ଇମେଲ୍ କରିବା 'to email'; often just ମେଲ୍.
Takes respectful endings like a person: କ୍ଲାଏଣ୍ଟଙ୍କୁ, କ୍ଲାଏଣ୍ଟ କହୁଛନ୍ତି.
Before an ending the hasanta drops: ମ୍ୟାନେଜରଙ୍କୁ. Many people say ବସ୍ 'boss' — same spelling as 'bus'.
Used everywhere, alone or after a surname: ମହାନ୍ତି ସାର୍. With endings: ସାରଙ୍କୁ.
The female counterpart of ସାର୍: ଦାସ ମ୍ୟାଡାମ୍.
Formal partner of ଦରକାର: ଆପଣଙ୍କ ଦସ୍ତଖତ ଆବଶ୍ୟକ.
Formal/office partner of କହିବା: ମୁଁ ଆପଣଙ୍କୁ ଜଣାଇଦେବି 'I'll let you know'.
ଏ ବିଷୟରେ 'about this (matter)'; also the 'Subject:' line of a letter or email.
ପରାମର୍ଶ ଦେବା 'to advise', ପରାମର୍ଶ ନେବା 'to take advice'.
ଶୁକ୍ରବାର ସୁଦ୍ଧା 'by Friday'. Compare ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ 'until'.
କାମ ବାକି ଅଛି 'there's work left'; ବାକି କାମ 'the rest of the work'.
The word in notices, news and minutes; in speech people say ମିଟିଂ.
ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ନେବା 'to decide' (lit. take a decision); passive ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ନିଆଗଲା 'it was decided'.
Heading of an office notice. ସୂଚନା ଦେବା 'to inform'.
ଛୁଟି ଦରଖାସ୍ତ 'leave application'. A more formal word is ଆବେଦନ.
ଛୁଟି ମଞ୍ଜୁର ହେଲା 'the leave was approved'; ମଞ୍ଜୁର କରିବା 'to approve'.
'Dear Sir' in applications and letters; to a woman ମହୋଦୟା. Never said aloud to someone's face.
Formal: ସାକ୍ଷାତକାର.
ମୋର ଦୁଇ ବର୍ଷର ଅଭିଜ୍ଞତା ଅଛି 'I have two years' experience'.
Indian English 'biodata'; ରିଜ୍ୟୁମ୍ is also heard.
ମୁଁ ସୋମବାର ଯୋଗ ଦେବି 'I'll join on Monday'. Inflect ଦେବା: ଯୋଗ ଦେଲି, ଯୋଗ ଦେଇଛନ୍ତି.

phrases.note: People also just say ୱାର୍କ ଫ୍ରମ୍ ହୋମ୍.

phrases.native: ମୁଁ ଟିକେ ବ୍ୟସ୍ତ ଅଛି, ପରେ କଥା ହେବା କି?
phrases.roman: muṃ ṭike byôstô ôchhi, pôre kôtha heba ki?
phrases.en: I'm a bit busy — can we talk later?
Good morning, sir — may I come in?
phrases.note: The standard way to enter a senior's cabin.

phrases.en: Please keep me posted on this. (polite)

phrases.native: ମୁଁ ଆଜି ସଞ୍ଜ ସୁଦ୍ଧା ରିପୋର୍ଟ ପଠାଇଦେବି।
phrases.roman: muṃ aji sôñjô suddha riporṭ pôṭhaidebi.
phrases.en: I'll send the report by this evening.
That's my responsibility, I'll take care of it.

phrases.native: କାମ ପ୍ରାୟ ସରିଗଲା, ଟିକେ ବାକି ଅଛି।
phrases.roman: kamô prayô sôrigôla, ṭike baki ôchhi.
phrases.en: The work's almost done, there's just a bit left.
Could the deadline be pushed back a little?

phrases.native: ଆଜି ମୋର ଦେହ ଭଲ ନାହିଁ, ଅଫିସ୍ ଆସିପାରିବି ନାହିଁ।
phrases.roman: aji morô dehô bhôlô nahiṃ, ôphis asiparibi nahiṃ.
phrases.en: I'm not well today, I can't come in to the office.
When would I start? (lit. when shall I join?)

grammar.title: Formal register in full: ଆପଣ, ସାର୍, ଆଜ୍ଞା and office Odia
grammar.body:
Odia shows respect in **three places at once**: the verb, the way you address people, and the words you choose. At work, with officials and in writing you switch all three.

**1. The verb: ଆପଣ forms in every tense.** You know most of them; here they are together:
Present: ଆପଣ କରନ୍ତି · Continuous: କରୁଛନ୍ତି · Past: କଲେ · Perfect: କରିଛନ୍ତି · Past perfect: କରିଥିଲେ · Future: କରିବେ · Command: କରନ୍ତୁ · 'Is / are': ଆପଣ ଅଛନ୍ତି, ନାହାନ୍ତି.
The **same forms** are used for a third person you respect, whose name takes **-ଙ୍କ / -ଙ୍କୁ**: ମ୍ୟାନେଜରଙ୍କୁ କହିଲି, ସାର୍ ମିଟିଂରେ **ଅଛନ୍ତି**, ମ୍ୟାଡାମ୍ **ଆସିଛନ୍ତି**. Using ସେ ଅଛି for your boss sounds rude.

**2. Address.** Spoken: **ସାର୍ / ମ୍ୟାଡାମ୍**, alone or after a surname (ମହାନ୍ତି ସାର୍, ଦାସ ମ୍ୟାଡାମ୍). **ଆଜ୍ଞା** is 'yes, sir' — very respectful, standard in government offices. Colleagues a little older than you get **ଭାଇ / ଅପା** after their name. In writing: **ମହୋଦୟ / ମହୋଦୟା** 'Dear Sir / Madam', closing **ଆପଣଙ୍କ ବିଶ୍ୱସ୍ତ** 'Yours faithfully'.

**3. Words.** Formal Odia prefers Sanskrit-based words: ଦରକାର → **ଆବଶ୍ୟକ**, କହିବା → **ଜଣାଇବା**, ମିଟିଂ → **ବୈଠକ**, ଚିଠି → **ଦରଖାସ୍ତ / ଆବେଦନ**, plus **ଦୟାକରି** and **ଅନୁରୋଧ**. Requests use the future (**କରିବେ**) or, in writing, **-ବାକୁ ଅନୁରୋଧ**: ଛୁଟି ମଞ୍ଜୁର କରିବାକୁ ଅନୁରୋଧ.

**Who uses what.** Seniors usually call juniors by name with **ତୁମେ** (ଆସ, ବସ), while juniors answer with **ଆପଣ** — even if the boss is younger. Colleagues of the same level use ତୁମେ, close friends ତୁ. In private-sector offices the vocabulary is full of English (ମିଟିଂ, ଡେଡଲାଇନ୍) — that's fine; the respect is carried by the **verb forms and address**, not by avoiding English.

**The trap:** don't mix levels inside one sentence: ~~ଆପଣ ଟିକେ ବସ~~ → ଆପଣ ଟିକେ **ବସନ୍ତୁ**; ~~ସାର୍ ଆସିଲା~~ → ସାର୍ **ଆସିଲେ**.

examples.en: Sir, are you coming to the meeting?
Madam is in a meeting at the moment.

examples.native: ମହୋଦୟ, ମୁଁ ଆପଣଙ୍କୁ ଜଣାଉଛି ଯେ ମୁଁ ଅସୁସ୍ଥ ଅଛି।
examples.roman: môhodôyô, muṃ apôṇôṅku jôṇauchhi je muṃ ôsusthô ôchhi.
examples.en: Dear Sir, I wish to inform you that I am unwell.

examples.native: ଦୟାକରି ମୋତେ ଦୁଇ ଦିନର ଛୁଟି ମଞ୍ଜୁର କରିବେ।
examples.roman: dôyakôri mote dui dinôrô chhuṭi môñjurô kôribe.
examples.en: Kindly grant me two days’ leave.
What is your view on this?
Yes sir, I'm sending it right now.

grammar.title: The passive and 'it can't be done': ନିଆଗଲା, ପଠାଯାଇଛି, କରି ହେବ ନାହିଁ
grammar.body:
Spoken Odia usually avoids the passive. It uses the active with an unnamed 'they', or a **ହେବା** verb (unit 25): ମିଟିଂ ବାତିଲ **ହେଲା** 'the meeting got cancelled', ଛୁଟି ମଞ୍ଜୁର **ହୋଇଗଲା** 'the leave was approved'. But office emails, notices, news and announcements love the **true passive**, and bosses use it too.

**How to build it:** stem + **-ଆ** + **ଯିବା**, and only ଯିବା changes for tense:
କରିବା → **କରା**ଯିବ 'will be done', **କରା**ଗଲା 'was done', **କରା**ଯାଇଛି 'has been done'
ଦେବା → **ଦିଆ**ଯିବ · ନେବା → **ନିଆ**ଗଲା · କହିବା → **କୁହା**ଗଲା · ଲେଖିବା → **ଲେଖା**ଯାଇଛି · ପଠାଇବା → **ପଠା**ଯାଇଛି · ଦେଖିବା → **ଦେଖା**ଯିବ · ଜଣାଇବା → **ଜଣା**ଯିବ
The verb is always **third person**, agreeing with the thing: ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ନିଆଗଲା 'a decision was taken' = 'it was decided'. 'By someone' is **ଦ୍ୱାରା** (formal, mostly written): ମ୍ୟାନେଜରଙ୍କ ଦ୍ୱାରା.

**Two everyday uses:**
- **ଦେଖାଯାଉ** 'let's see' (lit. let it be seen) and **ଦେଖାଯିବ** 'we'll see' — heard in every meeting.
- Notices: **ସୂଚନା ଦିଆଯାଉଛି ଯେ …** / **ଜଣାଯାଉଛି ଯେ …** 'it is hereby notified that …'.

**Can / can't be done: -ଇ + ହେବ.** The -ଇ form plus ହେବା makes an impersonal 'can': ଏହା ଆଜି **କରି ହେବ ନାହିଁ** 'this can't be done today', ଡେଡଲାଇନ୍ **ବଢ଼ାଇ ହେବ** କି? 'can the deadline be extended?' It is how people say no at work without saying 'I won't'.

**The trap:** for 'I was told / I was given' the person goes in the **dative**, not as the subject: **ମୋତେ** କୁହାଗଲା, **ମୋତେ** ଦିଆଗଲା — never ~~ମୁଁ କୁହାଗଲି~~.

examples.native: ବୈଠକରେ ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ନିଆଗଲା ଯେ ପ୍ରୋଜେକ୍ଟ ଆସନ୍ତା ମାସରେ ଶେଷ ହେବ।
examples.roman: bôiṭhôkôre nispôtti niagôla je projekṭ asônta masôre sesô hebô.
examples.en: It was decided at the meeting that the project will finish next month.

examples.native: ସମସ୍ତ କର୍ମଚାରୀଙ୍କୁ ଜଣାଯାଉଛି ଯେ ଶୁକ୍ରବାର ଅଫିସ୍ ବନ୍ଦ ରହିବ।
examples.roman: sômôstô kôrmôchariṅku jôṇajauchhi je sukrôbarô ôphis bôndô rôhibô.
examples.en: All staff are hereby informed that the office will be closed on Friday.
I was told the meeting is at ten.

examples.native: ଏ କାମ ଆଜି କରି ହେବ ନାହିଁ।
examples.roman: e kamô aji kôri hebô nahiṃ.

dialogue.title: Monday morning in Infocity
dialogue.setting: An IT company in Infocity, Patia (Bhubaneswar). Priyanka and Sourav are teammates of the same age (ତୁମେ); their manager is Mr Mohanty, who calls them by name and is answered with ଆପଣ and ସାର୍.

lines.speaker: Priyanka
lines.native: ଗୁଡ୍ ମର୍ଣ୍ଣିଂ, ସୌରଭ! ୱିକେଣ୍ଡ୍ କେମିତି ଗଲା?
lines.roman: guḍ môrṇiṅ, Sôurôbhô! wikeṇḍ kemiti gôla?
lines.en: Morning, Sourav! How was the weekend?

lines.speaker: Sourav
lines.native: ଆଉ କ'ଣ, ଦୁଇ ଦିନ ଶୋଇଲି। ତୁମ ରିପୋର୍ଟ ସରିଲା?
lines.roman: au kôṇô, dui dinô soili. tumô riporṭ sôrila?
lines.en: What else — I slept for two days. Is your report done?

lines.speaker: Priyanka
lines.native: ପ୍ରାୟ, ଟିକେ ବାକି ଅଛି। କିନ୍ତୁ ଶୁଣିଲ? ଡେଡଲାଇନ୍ ଗୁରୁବାର କରାଯାଇଛି।
lines.roman: prayô, ṭike baki ôchhi. kintu suṇilô? ḍeḍlain gurubarô kôrajaichhi.
lines.en: Almost, there's a bit left. But did you hear? The deadline's been moved to Thursday.

lines.speaker: Sourav
lines.native: କ'ଣ? ଶୁକ୍ରବାର ତ ମୋର ଛୁଟି ନେବାର ଥିଲା! ଭଉଣୀର କଲେଜ ଆଡମିସନ ପାଇଁ ସମ୍ବଲପୁର ଯିବି।
lines.roman: kôṇô? sukrôbarô tô morô chhuṭi nebarô thila! bhôuṇirô kôlejô aḍmisôn paiṃ Sômbôlpurô jibi.
lines.en: What? I was going to take Friday off! I have to go to Sambalpur for my sister's college admission.

lines.speaker: Priyanka
lines.native: ମହାନ୍ତି ସାରଙ୍କୁ ଏବେ ହିଁ ପଚାରିଦିଅ। ଆଜି ସେ ଭଲ ମୁଡରେ ଅଛନ୍ତି।
lines.roman: Môhanti sarôṅku ebe hiṃ pôcharidiô. aji se bhôlô muḍôre ôchhônti.
lines.en: Ask Mohanty sir right now. He's in a good mood today.

lines.speaker: Sourav
lines.en: Good morning, sir — may I come in?

lines.speaker: Mr Mohanty
lines.native: ହଁ, ଆସ ସୌରଭ, ବସ। କ'ଣ କଥା?
lines.roman: hôṃ, asô Sôurôbhô, bôsô. kôṇô kôtha?
lines.en: Yes, come in Sourav, sit down. What is it?

lines.speaker: Sourav
lines.native: ସାର୍, ଶୁକ୍ରବାର ମୋର ଗୋଟିଏ ଦିନର ଛୁଟି ଦରକାର ଥିଲା। ଘରେ ଟିକେ ଜରୁରୀ କାମ ଅଛି।
lines.roman: sar, sukrôbarô morô goṭie dinôrô chhuṭi dôrôkarô thila. ghôre ṭike jôruri kamô ôchhi.
lines.en: Sir, I was hoping for a day's leave on Friday. There's something urgent at home.

lines.speaker: Mr Mohanty
lines.native: ଶୁକ୍ରବାର? କିନ୍ତୁ କ୍ଲାଏଣ୍ଟଙ୍କୁ ରିପୋର୍ଟ ଗୁରୁବାର ସୁଦ୍ଧା ପଠାଯିବା କଥା।

lines.en: Friday? But the report is supposed to go to the client by Thursday.

lines.speaker: Sourav
lines.native: ଆଜ୍ଞା, ମୁଁ ବୁଧବାର ସୁଦ୍ଧା ମୋ ଅଂଶ ସାରିଦେବି, ଆଉ ପ୍ରିୟଙ୍କା ବାକି ଦେଖିନେବେ।
lines.roman: agya, muṃ budhôbarô suddha mo ôṅsô saridebi, au Priyôṅka baki dekhinebe.
lines.en: Yes sir, I'll finish my part by Wednesday, and Priyanka will handle the rest.

lines.speaker: Mr Mohanty
lines.native: ଠିକ୍ ଅଛି, ଛୁଟି ମଞ୍ଜୁର। କିନ୍ତୁ ପୋର୍ଟାଲରେ ଦରଖାସ୍ତ ଦେଇଦିଅ, ଆଉ ଫୋନ ଅନ୍ ରଖିବ!
lines.roman: ṭhik ôchhi, chhuṭi môñjurô. kintu porṭalôre dôrôkhastô deidiô, au phonô ôn rôkhibô!
lines.en: All right, leave granted. But put the application in on the portal — and keep your phone on!

lines.speaker: Priyanka
lines.native: କ'ଣ ହେଲା? ମଞ୍ଜୁର? ତେବେ ଆଜି କ୍ୟାଣ୍ଟିନରେ ଚା ତୁମ ତରଫରୁ!
lines.roman: kôṇô hela? môñjurô? tebe aji kyaṇṭinôre cha tumô tôrôphôru!
lines.en: So? Approved? Then today's canteen tea is on you!

culture:
Odisha has two very different work worlds. In **government offices** — the Secretariat (Lok Seva Bhavan), district collectorates, banks, schools — Odia is the official language, letters and notices are written in formal Odia, people answer seniors with **ଆଜ୍ଞା**, and a written **ଦରଖାସ୍ତ** is expected for almost everything. In the **IT parks and private companies** of Infocity and Patia in Bhubaneswar, the vocabulary is mostly English and colleagues switch between Odia, Hindi and English depending on who is at the table — but the Odia verb forms still mark respect.

Surnames are common forms of address: **ମହାନ୍ତି ସାର୍**, **ପଣ୍ଡା ସାର୍**, **ଦାସ ମ୍ୟାଡାମ୍**. Never call a senior by first name alone. A colleague a few years older is **ଭାଇ** or **ଅପା** after the name (ଶୁଭମ ଭାଇ, ଲିପି ଅପା). Bosses often use ତୁମେ to juniors; answering in kind would be cheeky.

Tea breaks (**ଚା ବ୍ରେକ୍**) are where the real talk happens. Joining a new job, a promotion or a wedding in the family means a box of sweets for the office. Leave is usually asked for in person first and then put in writing; around Raja (mid-June) and Durga Puja offices empty out, so ask early. A formal leave letter opens with **ମହୋଦୟ**, states the **ବିଷୟ**, asks with **ଦୟାକରି … ମଞ୍ଜୁର କରିବେ**, and closes with **ଆପଣଙ୍କ ବିଶ୍ୱସ୍ତ** and your name.

lessons.title: Small talk with colleagues

tip.title: Office Odia: English noun + Odia verb
tip.body:
- Work words are mostly English: ମିଟିଂ, ଇମେଲ୍, ରିପୋର୍ଟ, କ୍ଲାଏଣ୍ଟ.
- The **Odia verb** does the grammar: ଇମେଲ୍ **କରିବା**, ମିଟିଂ **ଅଛି**.
- Case endings go straight on the English word: ମିଟିଂ**ରେ**, ପ୍ରୋଜେକ୍ଟ**ରେ**, କ୍ଲାଏଣ୍ଟ**ଙ୍କୁ**.

tip.title: Going formal: ଆପଣ forms + ସାର୍ / ଆଜ୍ଞା
tip.body:
- To a senior, use **ଆପଣ** forms in every tense: ଦେଖିଲେ, ଅଛନ୍ତି, ଆସିବେ.
- The **same forms** for a senior you talk *about*, plus **-ଙ୍କୁ**: ମ୍ୟାନେଜରଙ୍କୁ କହିଲି; ସାର୍ ଆସିବେ.
- Address: **ସାର୍ / ମ୍ୟାଡାମ୍**; 'yes sir' = **ଆଜ୍ଞା**.
- Formal words: ଆବଶ୍ୟକ, ଜଣାଇବା.

lessons.title: Deadlines and getting it done

tip.title: By when, and finishing
tip.body:
- **ସୁଦ୍ଧା** = by (a deadline): ଶୁକ୍ରବାର ସୁଦ୍ଧା. **ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ** = until.
- **ସାରିବା** 'finish (something)': ମୁଁ ରିପୋର୍ଟ **ସାରିଲି**. **ସରିବା** 'be over': ମିଟିଂ **ସରିଲା**.
- **ବାକି** 'left': କାମ ବାକି ଅଛି.
tip.pattern: day + ସୁଦ୍ଧା  ·  ମୁଁ + thing + ସାରିବି  ·  thing + ସରିଲା

new: ମୁଁ ଆଜି ସଞ୍ଜ ସୁଦ୍ଧା ରିପୋର୍ଟ ପଠାଇଦେବି।
କାମ ପ୍ରାୟ ସରିଗଲା, ଟିକେ ବାକି ଅଛି।

tip.title: The passive: stem + -ଆ + ଯିବା
tip.body:
- କରିବା → **କରା**ଯିବ / **କରା**ଗଲା; ନେବା → **ନିଆ**ଗଲା; ଦେବା → **ଦିଆ**ଯିବ; କହିବା → **କୁହା**ଗଲା; ପଠାଇବା → **ପଠା**ଯାଇଛି.
- Always third person: ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି **ନିଆଗଲା** 'it was decided'.
- 'I was told' = **ମୋତେ** କୁହାଗଲା.
- **-ଇ ହେବ ନାହିଁ** = can't be done.

tip.title: Asking for leave, spoken and written
tip.body:
- Spoken: **ସାର୍, ମୋର ଦୁଇ ଦିନ ଛୁଟି ଦରକାର।**
- Written (ଦରଖାସ୍ତ): open with **ମହୋଦୟ** (to a woman ମହୋଦୟା), use **ଆବଶ୍ୟକ** for ଦରକାର, ask with **ଦୟାକରି … ମଞ୍ଜୁର କରିବେ**, sign off **ଆପଣଙ୍କ ବିଶ୍ୱସ୍ତ**.
